title: Chandrayaan-3
summary: Chandrayaan-3 was India's third lunar exploration mission and the first to achieve a soft landing on the Moon, following an earlier attempt, Chandrayaan-2, whose lander crashed in 2019 after a software issue during final descent. Chandrayaan-3 reused the successful orbiter design from Chandrayaan-2 but replaced the lander and added new sensors and stronger legs intended to tolerate a harder touchdown. The mission consisted of a propulsion module, a lander named Vikram (after Vikram Sarabhai, regarded as the founder of the Indian space programme), and a small rover named Pragyan.

instruments.name: ChaSTE (Chandra's Surface Thermophysical Experiment)
instruments.purpose: Measures temperature just below the lunar surface near the south pole

instruments.name: ILSA (Instrument for Lunar Seismic Activity)
instruments.purpose: Detects moonquakes and other surface vibrations

instruments.name: RAMBHA (Langmuir Probe)
instruments.purpose: Studies the thin plasma environment near the lunar surface

instruments.name: APXS and LIBS (on Pragyan rover)
instruments.purpose: Determine the elemental composition of lunar soil and rock

timeline.event: Launch from Sriharikota aboard the LVM3 rocket
Lander module separates from the propulsion module
Vikram lander performs a soft landing near the lunar south pole
Pragyan rover rolls out to begin surface operations
Lander and rover placed into sleep mode ahead of the lunar night

discoveries: Confirmed variation in subsurface temperature close to the lunar south pole
Detected sulfur and other elements in the soil at the landing site
Made India the fourth country to achieve a soft lunar landing and the first to land this close to the south pole
notes: The success of Chandrayaan-3 was widely seen in India as redemption for the Chandrayaan-2 lander crash, and the landing site was later named Shiv Shakti Point. Both the lander and rover completed their planned one lunar-day mission and were not designed to survive the extreme cold of the lunar night.
